[quote=koranvistan;61419367]Elena nodded, [i]"Good, good. You know how things can never cease, so I may be pulled for a meeting or two."[/i] She chuckled dryly.
She checked her watch and cleared her throat, getting the attention of the Family, [i]"The staff are preparing a light lunch now, it should be ready in maybe half an hour? Galina here will show you to where you'll be staying, and a member of staff will be present in the office at the end of the hall should you need anything. The table will be set in 40, if you choose to meet me down there. Feel free to roam, or ask the staff where things may be. I'll have a more formal tour for you once you're all settled."[/i]
She nodded curtly and began down the hall, into another room and out of plot relevance for now.

Galina led the family through the Palace's East Wing, to a set of double doors. [i]"This is Riverview Suite, it has big windows and good view of the river. Big, central sitting room with books, a porch, all nice things. I'll be in that office down the hall, can I get you all anything?"[/i]

She opened the doors, reavealing a gallantly decorated space. Landscapes from famous Elseyran painters, beautiful emerald curtains, and fine gold trim everywhere one could look. There were green couches and chairs built out of beautiful finished wood, with soft cushions and the occasional decorative throw blanket. The sitting room had not yet gotten so modern as to have a television, but it did boast towering oak bookshelves, full of publications in several languages from several centuries.

There were 6 bedrooms, a modest dining room, and a kitchenette. Four of the bedrooms were in the suite's loft, while the dining room and kitchenette sat opposite the bedrooms off the sitting room.[/quote]

Kain smiled understandingly. [i]"Yes, good luck with things that may come up."[/i]

The royal family followed Galina throughout the halls, and when the large double doors were opened, they took a few moments to admire the extravagant chamber. The lack of a television was not an issue, as they did not watch it.

The Corzerranean king approached Galina. [i]"I thank you, and Queen Elena, for this most elegant lodging provided."[/i]

Meanwhile, the twin guards set down the luggage of the family and began to unpack. The princes and princess took possession of their belongings from them. The Queen moved to join Zachariasz at his side.

[quote=koranvistan;61419367][i]"From the skies? I really am loved,"[/i] She chuckled, [i]"It's cold out here, would you like to come in? The Royal Family arrived about ten hours ago."[/i] She opened the door for Cecilia and followed. Elena gave her girlfriend a quick kiss after hanging her coat up. [i]"Can I get you something before we join everyone? I think the night may be coming to a close soon."[/i] She smiled warmly, and her cheeks were flushed. Her braid was starting to show signs of giving out, and her squint gave away how tired she was.[/quote]

Cecilia beamed. [i]"If it wouldn't be too much of an issue, would some coffee be available? Preferably with milk and a bit of sugar."[/i]

After a few moments, she took notice of Elena's tired state. [i]"Are you doing alright? If need be, I can help you with some arrangements. Please, don't wear yourself out."[/i] She gently cupped Elena's cheek with the palm of her hand. [i]"It seems like you've been working too long. Have you been working all ten hours the royal family has been here?"[/i]

The stadium flipped in an instant, the Floueschia bench leaping to their feet as the winger sprinted toward the supporters, pounding his chest before sliding on his knees in front of them. A half-cleared ball dropped invitingly at the edge of the box to their attacking midfielder, who struck it first time with venom. The shot dipped and swerved through a forest of legs before smashing into the net. Chaos followed. He tore off toward the sideline, teammates chasing him down as the crowd exploded, while Ardella players stood frozen, hands on heads, disbelief written all over their faces. From control to collapse, Ardella watched it slip away in the cruelest late twist, as Floueschia sealed a dramatic 21 victory

[Spoiler=Valddera vs Alaqar]Valddera edged out Alaqar in a tightly contested battle that simmered before bursting into life at key moments. The breakthrough arrived in the 27th minute when Maarash Ilvand carved his name into the match, latching onto a clever forward pass just outside the box. With a quick shift to create space, he unleashed a precise, low strike that kissed the inside of the post and rolled in. He turned immediately to the stands, pointing skyward before being embraced by teammates as Valdderas supporters roared with approval.The game settled into a tense rhythm after the break, but Valddera struck again in the 66th minute through Sulayev. The move built patiently, almost like a slow-burning fuse, before a sharp cross whipped into the area found him perfectly positioned. Rising above his marker, he powered a header down into the net, leaving the keeper rooted. Sulayev sprinted toward the corner, thumping the badge as the crowd swelled behind him, sensing control was firmly in Valdderas hands. But Alaqar refused to fade quietly. Just seven minutes later, in the 73rd minute, Ergash ignited hope with a sudden spark. A loose ball fell kindly on the edge of the area, and he struck it cleanly on the half-volley, sending it skimming past defenders and into the bottom corner. The Alaqar bench erupted, and Ergash celebrated with a fierce fist pump, rallying his teammates for one last push. The final minutes turned into a storm of pressure, Alaqar throwing everything forward while Valddera dug in, defending with grit and discipline. When the whistle finally cut through the tension, it was Valddera who emerged 21 winners, holding their ground in a match that felt like a tug-of-war right to the end.

Valddera 2 - 1 Alaqar

[b]Last Journey[/b]

It was another camping trip to the mountainside.

Well, technically they'd be sleeping in a lodge for a few days and camp outside from evening to morning between bits. It had begun back when the Rowans first built the lodge after getting the deed to the small plot of land in the start of the previous century and since then been visiting for holidays, events, and of course, family bonding.

The family car drove through the misty roads passing the pine trees. Gyles Rowan talked to his wife, Felice, about what road to take. One of the few cars in the traffic that afternoon. On the back of the car their children lazily looked out the windows, or at their phones.

No signal, no WiFi, no data.

Gyles Jr looked out the window, wire headphones on, mind thinking of college and time he could've spent with friends over family. By the other window, Winnie tapped away at her phone, the side of her face pressing against the window, trying to pass time with some idle offline app game.

Between them, the younger twins sat. Arthur, older by an hour of labour, was leaning by Winnie's arm, looking at her screen, he had insisted on the trip, since it's been a family tradition, especially now that grandpa was too old to make the trip and their uncles and aunts couldn't on a set time for a full family outing.

And then there's Nathan, the younger twin. He's staring at his own reflection on the visor, sometimes ahead on the road. He didn't want to come, like Junior, although for different reasons, he'd preferred to stay home and play for the short school break on the state. He, also, had no more battery on his phone.

The highway was driven on, and pines driven by, a cool morning wind passing by Gyles' driver's window, one harm out, holding a half smoked cigarette. His other hand on the wheel, and his phone showing directions. He had gotten the keys to the lodge for a week from his own father.

"When are we getting there." Nathan asked.

Gyles stopped talking to his wife about past trips, and kept his eyes on the road as he replied, "Ah, we're almost there. We're entering by this highway side, so it's different from when we," He paused to change lanes, a less busier one, "When we pick up your cousins, since we're not stopping by your godfather's house."

"Okay." Nathan replied, eyes drifting to the road ahead.

"We'll have burgers, marshmallows, a good bonfire, it'll be lovely, boys!" Felice said, looking briefly at them through the visor. Nathan didn't reply. "Although remember to listen to what your father says, it's not the full family, so we should stick together, okay? Especially by the river or in the forest." She continued.

"Pa, can we go fishing?" Arthur asked a bit louder, making Winnie wince. Gyles chuckled, "Maybe, maybe. Depends on the weather, maybe not, so don't get your hopes up, we'd have to use the lodge fishing rods." He told him.

Arthur would've replied, but then Gyles drove to the right, entering a dirt road that went between the pines and forestry, faint remains of old wooden fences bordering the old rock and dirt road. The twins sat impatiently for different reasons.

Eventually the wooden arch appeared, "Ah, welcome to the Rowdy Lodge." Felice said in a tune.

Gyles corrected, "Rowan, it's Rowan."

[b]Week's End[/b]

Nathan spent the arrival unpacking and trying to find somewhere to plug his charger, and then position his usb cable the right way, to charge his phone, although it was a task given his siblings and parents hogged the few that weren't already used. Thankfully he didn't have to resort to unplugging the fridge or telephone.

The mandatory fun consisted of trying to set up three tents between six people, three of which didn't have their hearts in it, and three clearly couldn't read the instructions right. Apparently the task was the intended fun, and not the results.

Bugs somewhat became an issue, although it was those inside the lodge. Winnie had complained, mostly scared out, about cockroaches or any fleas or whatever misinterpretation of what lived in the wilderness could crawl up her bed or tent. So she'd been constantly getting through the bugs pray.

They had lunch, burgers and fries. Then spent the afternoon a mix of napping and getting about. Arthur kept Nathan as his company, since their cousins weren't here and neither Junior nor Winnie had time, busy trying as ever if by miracle the signal had improved on the area.

By evening they finished setting the insides of their tents, and Gyles prepared a bonfire, although he had Nathan and Arthur pick up rocks, with Junior to help them. It was a stupid ordeal, to Nathan, and he did not like it, more than once confusing a bug for a stick or finding bugs under sticks.

Their return to camp was met with their father telling them stories when he was younger, this time without their uncles making him the end of the jokes, naturally giving his own version of his own childhood trips here. Felice and Winnie were in the lodge cooking, since not most of their food can be just done in the campfire.

They mostly had fish sticks, chicken nuggets, or hotdogs that night, as Arthur and their parents drew the other four into games and storytelling. Felice kept bringing the food, eventually just snacks, as they toasted marshmallows over the fire, fun at first, for the moment.

Some promises about fishing or shooting arrows were made.

Eventually they clocked into bed, as it got colder. They went away in groups of two, with their parents taking one tent, the young adult and older teenager taking the middle tent, and the young twins taking the last tent for themselves.

"Nat?" Arthur called out in the dark of the tent.

"Yes." Nathan replied from his sleeping bag.

"Do you think we'll catch anything this week?" Arthur asked him.

"Yes." Nathan replied.

"Really? What do you think we'll catch?" Arthur asked, turning around.

"Sleep, Archie." Nathan replied tiredly, although he found himself comical.

Arthur did so too, elbowing him with an unseen smile.

"Goodnight." Arthur said.

"Goodnight." Nathan replied.

[b]Promises[/b]

"But it's so fvcking humiiiiid." Winnie whined.

"You got boots. You got a coat. You got your hat. We're not making you kill the damned bird." Junior told his sister.

"No, you're just having me witness murder." She replied, narrowing her eyes, earning a glare from over their mother's shoulder.

"You two be quiet, we're not having this argument again." Felice said, as the three followed behind Nathan, Gyles and Arthur, whom held bows and arrows. As they say, to make a bowman, you start with their grandfather.

"Shhh!" Arthur shushed them from afar.

The group ventured further in, the morning was humid but sunny, none of the usual fog. Good enough to hunt. They had shot a rabbit although it wasn't quite big enough and it had gotten away, to Winnie's delight.

Gyles was happy, and a bit nostalgic. He was enjoying the trip, happy his wife indulged him over some trip to the mall or a park or her family. Yeah. Especially the latter. Arthur himself was happy because he genuinely likes camping and hunting, a family trait.

Nathan squinted his eyes, trying to find anything to shoot at, that he did like, shooting. Reminds him of some games he's played. He'd enjoy shooting at a tree but frankly wanted to catch something so they'd finally go back to the warmth of the lodge or campfire.

Their breakfast had been basically more s'mores, thus insufficient.

Nathan saw something that wasn't green, brown, or a mix of both, shaped animalistically, in the distance, and instinctively pulled the arrow in the string of the bow, aiming up, before letting go, just to be met with a solid sound.

"Uh, what was that?" Arthur got to Nathan's side, pressing himself against his brother. "Probably a rock, son." Gyles commented not far off.

"Tsk." Nathan frowned, putting the bow to his shoulder, and rushing away from Arthur, "I'll go fetch it." He said, walking over the sticks and leaves and grass of the forest. Arthur decided to quietly follow behind.

They were met by a pair of...odd statues, in the shape of what one might mistake as one feline with a man's face and what looked like a dragon, if the four legs are anything to go by.

"...what the fvck?" Nathan frowned, before Arthur stopped a bit breathless behind him, "Jesus, what... what's this?" The two approached the statues, between them was just...a stone floor, although there was a round hole, like a well without the surrounding walls, covered by some metal cap with some odd engravings.

"Whoa..." Arthur said, marveled. Nathan was just as awed, he knows the island is littered with old castles, old stuff all over, but he's never seen one up so close and without the entire class accompanying him over a school trip.

"Boys?" Gyles called out, approaching.

Nathan perked up, and decided to go find his arrow, looking around and between the statues. "Over here, pa!" Arthur waved his arm over, the sounds of four pairs of footsteps approaching reaching their ears.

By then Nathan found the arrow sticking by the side of the dragon statue, by the ground, buried into the stone. As he grabbed it, and repeatedly pulled on it, grunting, his family got to the vicinity.

"Hey, what did you guys find?" Junior asked.

Nathan pulled the arrow harshly from the ground, stumbling back, and falling down. Arthur turned around, as Nathan rubbed the back of his head, his other hand holding the arrow. Arthur was going to ask something, when there was a crack under Nathan.

He had landed on the iron thing in the middle.

"ARTHUR!" Junior grabbed Arthur, throwing him back and away from the stones.

Nathan felt something give in under him, to his panic, his eyes widened as he looked to Junior.

He faintly heard his name being screamed before he was falling down, rocks Pershing his fall, into some dark place.

Then pain, when he hit hard surface.

"NATHAN!!" Felice screamed her throat raw in one go, rushing past Junior to the edge, her husband immediately checking on Arthur, who was trying to check on his brother too, tears spilling from his eyes.

Winnie rushed to the group, "No, wait, stand back!" Gyles told her, turning then to Junior "Take Arthur back to the lodge and phone the poli-"

They would not be going back.

The ground crumbled around his wife who was peering down the edge, phone torch turned on, trying to look for her son.

"MOM!" Junior rushed in first, letting go of Arthur, who valiantly tried to rush in to save his mother from falling down too, their weights added, and in the panic, and the frenzy, Gyles rushed in too, as he saw his wife fall back, down, screaming.

He rushed to the grab and snatch his boys back, but by then the falling of the ground had reached them, he embraced them against himself, to shield them, he could only think what was happening, not comprehending.

Winnie saw as her family, her entire family, got swallowed into the pit, paralysed in terror, before she realised the ground was crumbling under her, trying and failing to step back, she fell on her back, and slid lower.

"HELP! HEEEELP!" She cried out, as she clawed and broke her nails against the stone, tears streaming down her face, before the stone gave in, and she was falling, the last thing she saw was the greying sky, the pine trees, and those two statues.

Then she fell with a painful thud.

[b]So below[/b]

Where are they?

What time is it?

Where is everyone?

"H-Hello?" Arthur asked around.

"Arthur!" Nathan rushed to the first voice to wake up, and then sound broke around them.

"Boys!" Felice shouted, heading for the voices.

"Mom!" They said, alongside a third voice, Winnie's. The four gathered.

"Feli!" Gyles rushed to his family.

"Where are we?" Junior was the last to huddle to them in the darkness.

Everyone took out their phones, shaking them to turn on their torches.

It was a designed cavern, mix of pillars and nature.

"Some... underground... tomb? Temple?" Winnie looked around, shining lights on the various statues and pillars.

Junior was staring up, frowning at the darkness. "It's dark out. We've been gone for at least the whole day." He muttered.

Felicia was checking on Nathan and Arthur, using her torchlight, meanwhile Gyles tried to get signal, anything, reception didn't find him. "Anyone got signal? Anything?" He asked them.

They all checked and came blank.

"Gyl, what do we do?" Felice asked, coming over to him.

"I don't know." He muttered with a frown, "Alright everyone" He said, deciding on some action over none, "Let's stick together, don't separate. We should explore a bit, maybe the place has an exit."

"This looks like a fvcking satanic cult basement." Winnie frowned.

"Winifred!" Felice said, "Language! Yes, even now." She sternly chastised, keeping her arms around Nathan and Arthur.

"Okay! Okay!" Winnie said, moving to standing to her oldest brother's side.

"I think I see only one path through those doors, but let's walk carefully, this place doesn't seem stable." Junior said, illuminating one of the least crumbled doorways.

"Alright, let us go. Follow me." Gyles said, taking the lead of the group. He had to get them safe. He had to get them home. He can't believe he's fvcked it up this bad, he shouldn't have wandered off the route. He shouldn't have lost sight of his children.

Felice was having similar thoughts.

[b]Unreliable Narrator[/b]

Six mortals wandered in the tomb of a forgotten forbidden thing, touching the ancient walls built by people and creatures that did not survive it, first in ages to wander in it.

They spent the first hours mapping the place in what battery they had in their phones. They eventually came upon rooms, and opened chests and tried to find clues. They didn't understand the languages, only snippets.

They found torches and kindling, tools and items. They mapped the first areas, and eventually decided to switch to the parchments to draw the maps they've made, to save battery and light, using torches lit by their lighters to light their way.

Hours passed, they found aged pots with wine, rotten food, and the odd strange looking bug the size of a penny they didn't recognise. They laughed, joked, and held eachother to distract themselves.

Just another family adventure.

They spent their first night there, they could tell it was nighttime because of Gyles' wrist watch, and slept in a room that might have been servant quarters once, on dusty beds they beat most of the dust out of, they slept in pairs, although some barely slept.

They awoke eventually, it was dark, and they had to turn on their phones and its torch lights to find the real torches and lit them, turning them off before continuing. The second day would not bring them the sought freedom.

They found stairs, holes, and cave ins that led down, but none that led up. No light from outside, no wind current, no water, no sound. Winnie would be the first to break in panic, but her parents and older brother reassured her.

Guilt ate at Nathan. Guilt ate at Felice. Guilt ate at Gyles. Hunger ate at all of them, fear was all they were fed outside those caskets of old wine, and what little water their cantines hand, and snacks they had in their pockets. They didn't want to go down.

The third day came after slightly better sleep. They felt optimistic, falling into exploring this floor. They found statues, and eventually, odd passages, hidden behind them and colourless banners, odd arrangements, they could not tell what this place was yet. If they did, they might not have felt as hopeful.

Eventually they had found clothes, things to use as tools, ropes, keys, mapped the first floor, they craft make makeshift things, craft what they needed, pocket what they could, pack what they can, eventually running of things to do, attempts to make, logic to draw, running out of excuses to not go down.

In the fifth morning, tiredness set in. Nobody was coming. They've been almost a week missing. Nobody has reached them yet. How long they had? They couldn't wait here months until people though of checking the lodge and then finding the trails towards the rapture where they fell, they'd starved and died by then.

Thinking, or rather not wishing to think, of no other options, they sort of agreed to go down. So down they went, all equipped and ready, all six of them, deeper into the old dungeon.

[b]Puzzling[/b]

Into darkness.

It was very much dark, rust and dust settled over almost everything. Winnie complained about it, her hair had to be tied back like her mother often has it. Gyles tried to keep it optimistic, drawing curiosity as one would to a mystery book, and like his father, Arthur would too.

Nathan found his company directed away from his twin to his more mature older brother, for Junior shared his worries and theories of where they were, they didn't find in themselves to complain or find the light side to their grin situation, they withdrew themselves to the back of the group behind their mother and sister.

As they had done above, they found many rooms with many things. But unlike the above, they had found locked doors, passageways, and odd manners of locks. Some keys they had worked, others worked on chests and wardrobes. Other doors and locks had to be opened by some kind of puzzle or twist or code.

They found more keys. And more tools. They found that odd wine. They found flasks and vials with odd very faintly glowing liquids they didn't touch. They found remains of dead bugs, slightly bigger than those above. All oddly shaped, not recognised by them. They found items and things to make torches out of. They found oil or what seemed like some form of primitive oil. They found rope, thread, wood, sticks, iron rods, and parchment. They mapped this floor.

They slept one night, and explored another day.

They slept a second night, but decided to leave after the third night, find if there was a below. They searched, prepared themselves, taking everything, even the odd flasks and vials, and eventually, indeed, there was a way down below, behind some sort of puzzle. One doesn't need to be bored with details, it was a lot of rock pushing and turning before something clicked and a wall lifted, and they were through it quickly.

It went down too. It went down, and they put it out of their minds, because to them it went forward, and forward was better than moving backwards. Down below they went, and they were met with much the same writ differently, slightly to the left in an odd manner.

Another floor, another map, another scavenger's hunt. They treated it like a game for now, a bit of a chore. But here the puzzles turned... strange. Sharp things, metal and stone, some statues short darts or arrows, there was some places where stepping would trigger something deadly to comw out. Although, it seems, some traps had living things intended, but the corpses of snakes hardly surprised the family. Clearly, the maker wasn't a welcoming sort.

Theories flew between them as a way of distraction. Junior and Nathan actually bothered to try and decipher things, to compare to what little they had known online. Eventually curiosity had damned them to time, hunger was running high, they had run of snacks, it's been over a week, what now? Eventually, it was Nathan who caved in, weak from hunger, he drank one of the vials, to his family's horror.

But hours, a day, passed, and no effects, no hurt, no pain, he felt better even. Then, he noticed his wounds and scratches from the fall didn't hurt, they weren't there at all, and with realisation he called these potions, no doubt. And potions, despite effects, are consumables.

The family drank, and then moved on to the next floor.

[b]Here Be Dragons[/b]

The bugs here were alive, and they hated them, and they hated back.

They had spent the first hours exploring rooms, seeing what keys worker and which didn't. They found a few holes by the walls, and from there they came. They hit them until they stopped moving, with arrows and rods and rocks.

Julian and Nathan would poke and break them to see what was inside, seems just usual bug stuff. Meanwhile they continued to explore, and fight now too. Room by room, faster than before, they went in pairs; Felice and Winnie, Gyles and Arthur, Junior and Nathan.

They found potions and pocketed them, they kept scouring and scavenging, mapping and noting down their finds. Eventually they had enough they piled off what was unnecessary onto some chests and such, before making base in a room by midday, whatever day it was now. They drank potions, some healed their bug bites, others energised them, based on colour. They also found glass balls, with no opening, filled with similar liquids. They took them too.

The next floor proved the same but slightly more difficult and bigger.

They would do much the same, although taking a stop to move useful things from the previous floor down if they had spent it. After testing those glass balls, turns out they had...odd effects. Some exploded, some exploded and lit something on fire, others let out some sort of poison gas, and others some sort of gas that paralysed, which they nastily found out when a thought dead bug awoke moments later to attack them from behind.

A floor cleared. A room prepared. Goods taken. Tools seized. Items crafted. Backpacks filled. And then they slept again once more.

By the next day, and next floor, Nathan and Junior had made the connections and compared to the roleplay tabletop dungeons and the historical ones from the age of heroes, but since the age of heroes lasted a thousand years, it could be as latest as the sixteenth century to as far back as the sixth century. But this did give them hope there was an exit, an end to this place.

And to Arthur, maybe some reward, which he repeated as some sort of encouragement as they moved to the next floor the next day. By then they had ran out of their modern arrows so they began reutilising the ones of the dungeon, although Felice and Winnie didn't have any arrows, they were good enough with using long rods as polearms, they didn't want to get close to the bugs.

As they went below, deeper down, the items and tools diversified, the world grew more detailed down there, the dungeon theory holding up, but it meant things would get harder, if not worse for them. So they prepared with that in mind, the possibility this was a dungeon instilled a possibility there was an after beyond this place, so forward they went, nowhere else to go but down another floor after another day.

Then they were met with monsters.

Odd things, grey or green things, malformed and likely inbred to hell. They came at then with clubs and stones, some had arrows, but, thankfully, they were scared of fire, and basically any resistance. After the first fright, they got more used to the buggers, but no less warning. They looted them, and for now, refused to cook and eat them, better relying on potions.

Arthur, Junior and Nathan felt it was like a game, for once the latter two felt it might be easier to survive here, compared to being trapped in an empty place. They might actually make it out of here.

[b]Fire & Iron[/b]

They were on a roll.

Monsters, it seems, fear and are hurt, usually, by one similar original thing; fire and hard or sharp things.

This is probably their second week down here, by then likely three weeks missing. Gyles held up that his brothers would be by now, if not by his own father figuring out his youngest son and his grandchildren not returning the keys of the lodge after an extra week, then at least by the lack of texts on the group chat trying to find out where he is, and initiating inquiries. They were, but Gyles wouldn't know that.

The floors did get harder, but it also made survival easier. Food in the form of potions, and they did try to cook and take a bite out of the bugs or critters, but didn't go down well, and they wasted a day by a very sick Junior, who swore the ever loving fvck out of the dungeon, but some potions saved him from dying to some magical supersh¡t.

They had taken to comforting eachother, mapping the floors, making camp, planning ahead, and thinking of the great tale they'd have for when they get out, for when they are rescued. Gyles would tell his brothers of his own great adventure he finally got to have that he had missed in his youth.

Felice would tell her family and friends and neighbours all about it, how brave her husband had been, how she finally got to do something close to cave diving as she had always wanted, and put her knitting and sewing skills to use. Junior would impress his friends and flaunt it at college, at parties, that he had been, if briefly, a true adventurer, although wishing to never go back here.

Winnie whined she'd never wish to put her nails through the suffering, but finally agreeing hunting did feel sort of nice, especially when Nathan loaned her his bow, she just wanted to tell her tale at school and social media, she hoped her friends missed her, and that if they find gold, she'd definitely buy herself her own car.

Arthur was chirpy and glad they were going good together, saying how he and Nathan would be the coolest boys in the school from there on, maybe they could apply to the Ministry of Magic or Law Enforcement or write a book or make a game based around what they experienced.

Nathan just repeated what Arthur said, although absentmindedly. He might like the idea of making a game about this, tho, that he did say honestly. But frankly, after this, he wanted to just stay indoors, eat, sleep, game, and relax until his back and feet didn't hurt, but he didn't say it aloud, he much enjoyed his twin's merriment, it was contagious.

Days passed, a third week went by, a week away from a month under here, a month since they went camping, so naturally, people should be searching by now. They went back up to the first floor, retracing their steps. They noted things they didn't spot before, and cleaned away some dead bugs to some empty rooms, and restocked. They waited a day before the debris before it rained a bit.

They collected water before deciding to continue their way out, it's unlikely they'll get signal or be heard from down here. They left to continue their march down a few more dungeon floors, heading for that twenty first floor and what awaited after it.

[b]Arthur Dies[/b]

Nathan was getting annoyed at the NPCs, sorry, the enemies of the dungeon. They weren't smart, but they sure as hell were strong, or at least those not the size of a toddler. Some had harder skin, some didn't but they made up in speed. And the spiders didn't help, or what looked like spiders. Four legs, many eyes; spider, right?

Winnie didn't like anything not bipedal and two-eyed, so Felice with her experience of house keeping and killing bugs, dealt with them with swift blows. Rod, broom, not much difference. Monsters could not crawl into holes, well, most of them, so they had to either fight, which they often did, or run away, which they often didn't. Gyles began getting more strict but no less paternal with them, after all, these enemies are armed, they could die. So they began making, crafting armour. The wooden armour attempts felt and looked silly, until Junior and Nathan pointed out leather also works. But nobody wants to skin and wear the tough skinned monsters. And skeletons didn't have skin.

Looting some proved to solve that but also wrong the problem these monsters had no design and no hygiene, the stench followed until they could clear the floor, and rest. How big was it? What did it do? What did it look like? How much armour? What weapon? How old? How strong? How fast? How flexible? Did it have some fictional or real life comparison? Did it spit or summon or do anything? Arthur and Nathan sometimes got into arguments over what was and wasn't like Minecraft mobs, which offended Nathan greatly, because he refuses to call the dungeon a nether dungeon.

"It is NOT a fvcking" He pulled an arrow from the eye socket of some...thing they had yet to label, but the arrowhead got stuck inside and so he angrily threw the stick away, "piglin!"

"No they do not! What are you even on about, pa?!" Arthur said, to Gyles' delight.

Junior rolled his eyes, and as the twins faced their father with arguments and confusion from the bait Gyles had guilefully delivered, Arthur went silent with a sudden sharp inhale.

Something sharp was sticking out of his right side, below his ribs.

"...Pa?"

Arthur fell forward, dropping the torch, which illuminated the critter behind him.

Nathan screamed and rushed, using his bow and attacking the creature. Gyles was already by him, as was Junior, Gyles immediately picked up Arthur as Junior went to hit the thing with a rod.

"No, no, no, Arthur, Archie, stay with me, Dad is here. Look at me." He cradled him as he knelt, over his lap.

"Pa, it hurts." Arthur winced, holding his sides, Gyles immediately reached out to cover it with his hand, to stop the blood flow.

"Shh, I'm here. I'm here. Stay with me. FELI! FELI!" He screamed out, as his other sons beat down the critter, even when it had gone down, they kept hitting him, over and over.

Arthur let out a cough, a quiet but wet cough that sprinkled blood over his lips and chin and shirt, causing Gyles' eyes to widen with dread. Nathan was panting with exertion, his bow broken in half, before Junior pulled him back, before going next to his father, searching his own bag for anything, anything to give Arthur.

"Gyles?" Felice was running down the corridor, Winnie holding a torch besides her mother, as they rushed over. "Dad! He's over there!" She spotted the four of them, and as Felice got closer, a cry left her throat, "NO!"

She was on Arthur immediately, holding his head between her hands, "No, no, no, my boy," She said quietly, tears already springing from her eyes, her throat closing, as her chest tightened with an agony she hadn't felt since Nathan fell down this place.

"Ma, Ma it hurts." Arthur said, staring up at her.

Gyles rummaged through her bag quickly, Junior started throwing everything out of his father's bag's also, alongside his own, seeking anything that could be used.

Nathan stood stupefied by them.

A thousand thoughts ran through his head. Disbelief, a total disbelief, a shock so profound he forgot to breathe until Winnie grabbed him by his shoulders.

"Are you alright?" She asked him firmly, he nodded rapidly, and she held him, hands on his shoulder, his back to her legs, and they watched.

They tried to clean the deep wound, made Arthur drink potion, after potion, covered the wound with healing potions too, before trying to close it. Eventually they went to their makeshift safe room.

They laid Arthur down on his bed, and continued to tend him. Gyles took his wife's hands into his, as she covered her mouth with her free hand. Junior came by Arthur's bedside and stroked his hair, with Winnie and Nathan lingering behind them.

"Hey there, Archie. How are you feeling?" Junior asked quietly, softly.

"... I'm...kinda cold." Arthur blinked slowly, he felt numb where he didn't feel pain. He blinked slowly again, "I'm kinda sleepy."

Felice's eyes watered but she wiped them, she pulled out a piece of cloth they had packed, forcing a smile, "Here, sweetie." She pulled it over Arthur, tucking him in as she had done not so long ago, "It'll all be alright." She kissed his forehead.

"Thanks, Ma..." Arthur said, smiling faintly, and drifted to sleep.

They stayed by him as he slept.

They stayed by him as he didn't awake.

Eventually, Julian was the first to go, and touch Arthur, search for a pulse, but he was met with cold flesh that was stiffening.

He closed his eyes to force down a cry of agony, before he turned around and nodded.

Felice's cry was visceral, as she threw herself over Arthur's body, crying her lungs out, Gyles had to look away, as he wept with her, coming over, embracing her from the side, looking over their dead son.

"No, no, no, not my boy, why him, no, oh God," She kept sobbing, and Gyles didn't have much to say, he didn't have anything but grief at heart, feeling the failure and agony press on him, as if it was suffocating the words out of him.

Junior walked over to Nathan and Winnie.

"Is he?" She asked.

Junior nodded, and Winnie gasped.

[i]No, it can't be, not Arthur.[/i] was all Nathan could think, staring at the calm and pale body of his twin, as Junior embraced him and Winnie, the latter crying onto her older brother's shoulder, sobbing audibly.

Nathan wept, but didn't make a sound.

[i]Arthur couldn't die.[/i]

[b]Stages[/b]

Gyles and Felice didn't let the kids leave the room for a while, they kept by Arthur's corpse for a while, before deciding to wrap him up, to push further off the argument they were about to have, and take care for their son's remains. The kids helped, for what they could.

They decided to cremate him, not let him rot down here, to not let him be found, unearthed, and eaten by whatever dwells down here. They've been officially missing for a month, by the time they had gotten to wrapping Arthur up, mourning him, carrying him to the first floor, and then burning him before the opened sky ruins.

They told the kids to stay up in a safe room up here in the first floor, where they stayed, quietly contemplating, remembering Arthur. They were trying to cope, mostly by trying to keep Nathan's mind off things. But Nathan's minds was on everything but Arthur yet everything was about Arthur, whom he had been with since birth, since forever, whom would've been with him until they grew old, whose children would've been cousins, gone together. Gone.

Below, their parents had an argument, finally breaking down. Blame was thrown, blame for the damned trip, blame for all that had happened in that marriage, insults and speculations, everything laid bare in the agony and grief of loss, until Felice's throat was too raw to scream, until Gyles had broken enough things that the knuckles of his fists had been bled.

After some acceptance, or at least understandment they had issues to solve, maritally and personally, they agreed to put that away. They couldn't loose another child. They would not. Not ever. They need to get out, they need to take this seriously, they no longer can rely on rescue, it's been a month, they had to go deeper, they had to finish this damned dungeon.

They no longer could go out in pairs, and they could no longer go without a plan.

So they went, fetched their children again, held them, and then explained the changes, the plans, the strategy, and as such. They mostly got the jist, Junior and Winnie understanding, they had to stick together. They had to keep eachother alive and aware.

Nathan half listened. He had a different sort of survival in mind. He wanted to kill everything, everyone, every beast and animal and insect in this damned dungeon, step and burn every plant, and make then suffer, and then, only then, did he want to get out, alive, in spite of this dungeon.

He didn't voice this.

They spent a quick trip down, back to the twenty and onwards levels. They first spent two days preparing, organising, and armouring themselves. They made orders, strict rules, and strategy, they organised what they heard and knew, and what to do. Chiefly, Nathan must be between the four of them at all times, Junior and Gyles on the vanguard, and Felice and Winnie on the rear.

Then they'd go out, for five days, the same system; unlock the next floor, enter, map everything, slowly clear the floor out, check for traps, check for hideholes, kill everything, check for anything alive, kill everything left, check again, then begin unlocking doors, chests, and such, ransack and scavenge everything, make a safe room, recollect, plan, and rest.

Then repeat.

More floors. More days.

A month and a half.

Only thirty five floors.

[b]Death[/b]

Tempers ran somewhat hot, after the forty fifth day down here, on the thirty fifth floor. Nathan was more uncontrollable, self blaming and yet blaming everyone, which they understood, he's young, his twin died right next to him, but it was getting irritating to Junior and Winnie.

Nathan tried to kill, shoot, and absolutely mutilate the enemies, sometimes throwing paralyzers to torture them, before killing them, which he was chastised for. Gyles, however, directed his anger to focus, same way Felice did her grief into solving these floors quicker.

And they did go through then quicker because of this. No stops, no wondering, not much chatting as there was planning, to hide or veil the grief and rage. Winnie did need the most comfort, as she seemed the most affected and reactive, crying periodically, which Junior tried his best to reassure that they would get out of here.

Nathan shared the sentiment for different reasons. He wanted to get out of here, more for the sake of proving something agains the dungeon than survival. His parents had similar but unsaid feelings, they'd be fine if their children got out at minimum.

Oddly enough after the thirty fifth floor, they were net with...a series of interconnected ten floors, by an open gallery, filled with odd stones that emitted light. A vast and large sort of gallery and library, with a withered garden at the bottom, and vines long since dear by the pillars. They stayed an entire day exploring, scanvanging. Their collection of keys proved useful, it seems they needed a handful to get through the remaining floors.

After going back and forth a full day, with all keys they ever found and more, they spend the entire day opening doors, and the last floors. The first one was a treasury, gold unimaginable, enough to make them momentarily forget the loss and lose themselves in greed before deciding to pocket some diamonds, anything high value, after checking it wasn't cursed, no need to die here from greed.

Then they were before what apparently was the penultimate door, more like a tall stone gate, because it just screamed exit. A very large but already solved puzzle room, with what seemed to be some sort of very old but not irrelevant dragon in the middle, chained and seemingly malnourished, facing some gate. Bones around him, and looking pained, his eyes unfocused and blind in the dark, gaunt and crusty.

They decided to find and bring everything they could, going about it smartly. Clearly the dragon guarded the gate. They didn't want to fight it, so they gathered all their paralyzing crystal bombs, and then threw them all at once, rapidly. The dragon reacted, yes, but not for long, soon ending stiff. Once it was certain it wasn't faking it, and the gas dissipated, they began throwing the poisonous bombs into his nostrils.

Throw in, run away, wait, and go back to throw more. They kept doing this over and over until absolutely certain, and when they felt the dragon no longer was paralyzed, they began hitting it in any soft spots they could find. Eventually driving many rods and such into his eyes as deep asthey could go, and into his armpits and belly. Eventually it was clear the dragon would not breathe a last at all.

Triumphantly, they celebrated, and rushed to the door.

The keyholes were different here, they were obviously not on the door, but small pillars in front of it, four pillars, with obvious hand and wrist sized holes, inside the holes were spikes. It didn't need much logical thinking to realise what they were.

Nathan didn't have much say in the following argument, he had gone into shell shock staring at the gate, the giant gate. Anger flared so much it hurted to feel it, his eyes didn't weep, but he scowled, fists tightly clenched at his sides. This wasn't fair. This wasn't fair at all. Was he to die? Was he to die like Arthur? He couldn't come back then, and enact revenge. He wanted to survive, he wanted to survive so badly.

This wasn't fair.

This wasn't fair.

But as he raged, his family debated, arguing, shouting. How to solve this? Grab a monster and put it here? It bore merit. They'd just be stuck there so they'd get out. Thus, they spent a day, going back floors, and grabbing and netting any critter and taking them to the pedestals. They died, from struggling, mostly, and it seems they didn't reach down what seemed to be the issue.

It was a sort of thing, like a lever, when pulled, kept your arm stuck in the thing. And the big ones sort of grabbed it, then tried to escape, thus bleeding themselves out in breaking their wrists and arms, and thus letting go of the device. By the forty eighth day they were stuck in the forty eighth floor. By the time enough bodies piled and it got tiring of grabbing and chopping bodies, the five, a hurtful thing to remember that they had been six, decided the thing obviously wanted them, or at least, the tools available weren't sufficient.

They decided to sleep on it.

Or rather, let Nathan sleep, as they came upon a decision through the night. Maybe they'd be stuck here, maybe not, but heavily betting on the former, they came to an agreement, although with some level of reluctance from the siblings, who had only begun their adulthoods, but the memory of Arthur's death and Nathan's own future chided them.

Their forty ninth morning came and they tried themselves, not leaving room for Nathan to argue his lungs out, impotent to their decisions, and it didn't hurt much, albeit it made them nervous. They didn't die, just locked themselves holding something and turning it to the puzzle instructions on the gate.

Which opened.

And beheld a natural staircase to some sort of pathway, to an elevated platform, where between some pillars at the center stood another pedestal, with some sort of red orb, all illuminated by what clearly was sunlight through some sort of exit upwards. He explored everything and found some sort of instructions in symbols on the pedestal and the columns.

Nathan was told to check things out with utmost care. So he did, checking everything out. Hours passed, as they stayed there, straining their legs, before stopping at midday, closing the door and conferring. Over the afternoon into the evening they planned and conferred they'll be able to let go of the handles and keep the door open if Nathan does as the instructions say.

So after a final meal of potions, and getting themselves ready, they spent the evening guiding Nathan into singlehandedly doing the puzzle. Moving the right pieces around the pedestal, clicking or moving the right hidden pieces or symbols. He did everything right, after a few tries, to the excitement of his family, he felt better rather than bitter, as he got the things done properly.

He did was he was supposed to.

So his confusion was natural when he finished, and heard the awful crunch of bone and flesh, followed by his family's screams. The doors didn't close, but their pedestals did, glowing red and the red light trailing over towards Nathan, past Nathan, to the red glass orb that slowly glew to life behind him.

He didn't check.

His eyes transfixed on his family.

They weren't just screaming, they were withering, rotting before his eyes, his pupils shrunk as his breathing came to a halt.

Belatedly, he realised, he was dying too.

His last sight was his family going limp, and then the cavernous ceiling above, and that red crystal orb.

Betrayal. Twisted betrayal, a hopelessness, a furious rage, that felt weaker and weaker. He wanted to get up, to struggle, he wanted to scream, but he felt paralysed. Staring at the cavern with no sky. It was unfair. He wanted to live. He wanted to kill everyone, everything, that had wronged him, taken everything from him, everyone from him, and his future.

He wanted to bitterly survive and live forever no matter what.

[b]Undeath[/b]

Agony.

Pure, unfiltered, raw agony.

[i]WHY. WHY. WHY. WHY. W HY. WHY. WH Y. WH Y. W HY. WH Y. WHY. W HY. WHY. W H Y.[/i]

He didn't understand. He didn't understand what he did wrong. Everything hurts. Everything is in pain. He feels it. He knows he's screaming. He can't stop. He's writhing on the ground.

[i]IT BURNS. IT BURNS. IT BURNS.[/i]

Nathan writhes on the ground, convulsing, as red mist floats down the red crystal orb, and like tendrils, enters his lungs, his pores, his flesh. And burns it, eats it, withers it, melts it, and rots away.

He screams for his father. He screams for his mother. He screams for his brother. He screams for his sister. He screams for Arthur.

He died. He had died. He saw the darkness. He saw the light. But something plucked him, something red, and seized him down, dragged him, he feared he was in hell. He didn't want to go to hell. He wanted to be with Arthur.

In truth, the phylactery had been fed endless souls, every critter they had sacrificed at those four altars, alongside, as it dragged Nathan from the afterlife back to this world and tethered him to it, fed upon the other souls here, every beast, alive or slain, and a fifth human soul, dragging them down like fuel to kindling, even the dragon's soul, which had been tormented in no way a creature of its excellence should be.

And drew all that power, all that life, all that death, into itself, and into Nathan.

Who screams, who claws at himself, flesh tearing by his own hands and the magic taking away his humanity. The pain flayed his nerves, literally. His emotions shifted, he begged for mercy, for the end, after running out of questions, he prayed, begged, implored for help, that didn't come.

The phylactery began then drawing the life force from the stones and ground of the dungeon and land above, trees withering, green turning to black and grey, birds and animals and bugs dropping dead, and then withering, all of the sudden.

And Nathan began to rage, boiling with fury, he cursed everything, everyone, and himself. He promised revenge, absolute and total vengeance, he swore and swore, and swore. He clawed at the ground, crawled over the pillar, trying to climb the pillar to get on his feet, but tumbling down with it.

The phylactery fell down, bouncing before moving itself, rolling next to, in front of Nathan, reflecting his countenance.

Nathan screamed again, his face rotting, aging, deteriorating, he tried to push away, get up, but then saw his hands, revealing bone. Then held his face.

How can he see without eyes?

Orbs of light shone in them.

He looked at himself on the orb.

How can he scream without a mouth?

He tried to breathe. He couldn't.

He tried to blink. He couldn't.

He tried to speak. He couldn't.

He tried harder. He willed it.

And then the world blinked.

But he had no eyelids.

When he 'opened' them a skull met him.

His skull.

He felt nothing anymore.

He felt calm, as he picked up the orb.

He held it, between his hands.

He stared at himself as flesh left his form, and clean bone remained.

And those bones grew, bigger than he ever was. Bigger than his father ever was. Bigger than he could've ever gotten had he lived

Ah.

[i]I'm dead.[/i]

And the phylactery flew into his ribcage and merged with his bones.

The subsequent agony made him scream.

He willed himself to have a voice.

And willed this pain gone.

His lichdom translated this into blowing the entire dungeon and a good part of the withered wildlife and forestry by the mountainside above the dungeon into nothing.

He was flung skywards, he left himself he tossed, as the explosion shook the island.

Alarms, magical and military, as well as civilian sirens and emergency systems sprung online.

Missing the thing that flew out of it, Vespurias officially declared after firm confirmation that somewhere in the Myst Isles' inland mountains and forest, a large explosion had occured.

Allies and the International Forum were informed, and all flights suspended in the area until it could be investigated.

A state of emergency was declared on the island by the state.

Nathan fell.

Nathan fled.

Nathan wandered.

He was going home.
